card: This PR adds an optional delay_for argument to sendrawtransaction, allowing users of private broadcast connections to defer initial transaction broadcast by a specified duration with randomized jitter. It aims to improve transaction privacy by making time-correlation tracking harder for network observers. All evidence for importance comes from the author description; no external issue or discussion is linked. Pending transactions are stored in-memory only and are lost if the node restarts before broadcast.
evidence: The author states in the PR description that the goal is "increased privacy, by making time-correlation-based tracking more difficult", pairing randomized delay with private broadcast to hide creation time alongside originator identity.
problem: Immediate transaction broadcast allows network observers to correlate transaction generation times with specific user actions or network events. Users relying on node-level privacy mechanisms cannot decouple transaction creation from broadcast timing without external scheduling tools.

risk.why: Logic flaws in transaction queuing or deferred broadcast could drop valid transactions, delay critical broadcasts indefinitely, or leak broadcast scheduling information.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the patch record; pending transactions are held in memory only and will not survive a node restart.
summary: Adds an optional delay_for parameter to the sendrawtransaction RPC to postpone initial transaction transmission when using private broadcast. Submitted transactions are placed in an in-memory queue and released by PeerManager after the requested delay plus randomized jitter. Transactions are validated both upon RPC submission and again before broadcast.
uncertainties: The patch diff was not provided in the record, preventing verification of queue management and concurrency safety.
The PR assumes private broadcast functionality is present and enabled, but no tracking issue or dependent PR is explicitly linked.
